findings.claim: The 'Request cookies are parsed leniently' wave decision lists `res.cookie` as one of the app-side calls where D-205's exception applies. NaruServe has no `res.cookie`. D-203 and the contract name the method `res.addCookie`, and `res.cookie` appears in docs/api only as the Express equivalent. An implementer could read this as a new method to add, or could leave `addCookie` out of the validation.

The decision keeps a request cookie value exactly as sent, even when it falls outside the RFC 6265 grammar. It limits D-205 validation to the constructor and setters. So the request Cookie objects must be built through a path that skips validation, and the decision never says whether `res.addCookie` re-checks name and value before it serialises. An app that echoes a request cookie (`res.addCookie(req.cookie("x"))`) could then emit a Set-Cookie whose value breaks the grammar, with no exception, despite D-205. Header injection is not possible here, because CR/LF and `;` cannot get through the parser.
findings.suggested_fix: State that `res.addCookie` checks the name and value against the D-205 grammar, so request-built cookies are checked too and throw there. Or state that the non-validating construction of request cookies is internal-only and record that in docs/api/cookie.md.

findings.claim: The decision says lenient parsing with the value 'kept as sent' 'matches Express's cookie-parser'. That is not true. cookie-parser parses through the `cookie` package, which percent-decodes each value with decodeURIComponent, and Express's res.cookie percent-encodes. An Express user who moves code over would expect decoded values. The decision states the opposite and calls it Express behaviour, and docs/api/cookie.md says nothing about encoding.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the claim that this matches cookie-parser, or adopt the cookie-parser behaviour: percent-decode on read when it decodes cleanly, otherwise keep the raw value. Either way, record the decoding rule in docs/api/cookie.md under the D-208 update.
